b940548a316b.text: Molecular components let a cell convert odor recognition into a measurable signal.

d7dbadb2a208.text: Explain the roles of OR, Orco and GCaMP in the AeroSense sensing chain.

dea402863bcd.text: Predict what happens when one required component is removed.

62af076d149c.text: Recognize why containment and biosafety matter for a living sensor.

746465c5940b.text: AeroSense does not transplant a fly’s nose into food. The plan is heterologous: selected insect odorant receptors, with Orco, expressed in HEK293 cells, with a GCaMP-class reporter that can turn a calcium change into light.

2860deab6939.text: That is an engineered information pathway. Fluorescence is still not a food verdict, and this lesson does not claim a working device in hand.

95e6c8548ae2.text: Recognition happens at the receptor. Measurement happens after a reporter converts that event into a signal.

7a52ee69be7a.text: Proposal-level assemblies keep construct details off the main path: Construct A is an OR–IRES–mCherry style expression cassette; Construct B is a GCaMP–Orco fusion style cassette. Exact maps, restriction sites, and cloning steps belong in Parts and Experiments — not here.

15b92eebe824.text: OR recognizes odorant. Orco partners with insect ORs so the receptor can function as a ligand-gated ion channel in this heterologous plan. GCaMP reports a calcium change as fluorescence.

959cf747edf4.text: mCherry, when used, is an expression marker — a way to see that a construct is present — not the odor-to-light conversion. A photodiode reads light outside the cell. An AI classifier, if used, sits even later, in computation.

3c127302c595.text: Published HEK insect-OR panels that combine Orco and GCaMP motivate this architecture. They are starting points, not drop-in proof that AeroSense DNA already works in the team’s hands.

527e1231b4b2.text: Assemble the biological sensing chain and place the detector and classifier in their layers. Select a part, then a zone, or drag with a pointer.

9fa9d3073fa3.text: HEK293, OR, Orco, and GCaMP belong in the cell. The photodiode belongs in readout, outside the cell. The AI classifier belongs in computation. mCherry can ride in the cell as an expression reporter; it is not required for the odor-to-fluorescence conversion.

af38c631bbdd.text: Conceptual assembly — not experimental AeroSense data and not a plasmid map.

c484aed2e10a.text: What is AeroSense’s planned biological sensing element?

2cd0aae2050e.text: Living HEK293 cells that express insect OR/Orco proteins and a calcium reporter.

28037eed6990.text: A photodiode that binds odorant molecules in place of a receptor.

ce13bb78ed9e.text: An AI classifier that is itself the living sensor.

3322d06a6862.text: The planned biological element is a living cell chassis (HEK293) that expresses insect odorant receptors with Orco, plus a GCaMP-class reporter. Optics and AI sit downstream. They are not the receptor.

59f136379d0e.text: What role does GCaMP play in this sensing chain?

b3828f263f0e.text: It binds odorants instead of the olfactory receptor.

05af2e3eee2d.text: It reports a calcium change as fluorescence, which can then be measured optically.

5676aafd72bb.text: It legally certifies food as safe once it glows.

096a44bf5cd6.text: GCaMP is a genetically encoded calcium indicator. In this design it converts a Ca²⁺ change that can follow receptor activation into a fluorescence readout. It does not bind the odorant in place of OR, and a glow is not a food certificate.

dad09280ed5c.text: Why is containment necessary for a living odor sensor?

7887ec79d7ba.text: Engineered living cells should stay physically isolated from food, users, and the open environment.

56d29a9df421.text: Containment is optional if the cells look healthy under a microscope.

02efee60e7d9.text: Containment exists so the AI can smell the room from outside the laboratory.

d9084b6b892d.text: HEK293 cells engineered to express heterologous receptors are living genetically modified material. They belong behind a sealed cartridge or other containment concept, with responsible handling and waste. They should not contact the food being screened.
